compiled_state.author: Joe Oakhart
compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

The CI repair loop cannot fix lint failures in any project that is not Python. When `run_checks` fails, `apply_ci_repair` short-circuits into a hardcoded autofix that shells out to `ruff check --fix .` on the activity worker. Three defects follow. It is hardcoded to one language, it measures success as "files changed" rather than "the failure is fixed", and it is unscoped, so it rewrites the whole tree.

Running the platform against the `archive-massgov-pfml` portal made the damage visible. Prettier flagged one TypeScript file, and the repair loop instead modified 16 unrelated Python files across five attempts with `llm_calls=0` on every attempt, so no agent ever saw the failure.

## Approach

Let each project declare its own fix command in its checks config, and run that command in the same pod and image the checks already run in, so the fixer sees the toolchain the checks saw.

This fits because the platform already solved the identical problem for the check itself. `checks/runner.py` builds a script and executes it through `gates/pod_runner.py`, so the fix path reuses that transport rather than inventing a second one. A project-declared command is also the only option that generalises across client tech stacks. The platform cannot know whether a repo wants `ruff`, `prettier --write`, `gofmt`, or a bespoke `make fix`, but the repo already knows. A project declaring no `fix_command` falls back to agent repair, so no existing project regresses.

### Bounding what a fix may write back

A verified fix is copied back only for files the failure summary named. `failing_files` extracts those paths, and `in_repair_scope` tests one changed file against them.

The empty-scope guard does not live in `in_repair_scope`. A per-file tester handed an empty scope matches every file, which is fail-open and is the whole-tree rewrite this ticket removes. The guard lives one level up, in `_apply_staged_files`, which returns 0 immediately when `scope` is empty, before it iterates `changed` at all. That placement makes the guarantee independent of whatever `in_repair_scope` returns for an empty scope, so the per-file default cannot defeat it.

Fail-closed is the right default. A command such as `npm run lint:fix` reformats every file it is pointed at, and a summary such as `[warn] Code style issues found in the above file(s).` names none of them. Fail-closed costs one autofix opportunity there and still reaches a fix through agent repair, whereas fail-open costs an unbounded diff.

### Observability

Every outcome is recorded, because the motivating incident was invisible. `_project_autofix` emits one structured log naming the path it took. Each outcome is derived from the `ChecksFixResult` that `run_fix` returns, carrying `verified`, `exit_code`, and `changed_files`, together with the scope tuple and the applied count.

| Outcome | Discriminator |
| --- | --- |
| `no-fix-command` | `config.fix_command` empty, tested before any pod is created |
| `pod-failed` | `run_fix` raised, caught by the existing `except Exception` arm |
| `fix-exited-non-zero` | `result.exit_code != 0` |
| `fix-changed-nothing` | `result.exit_code == 0` with `result.changed_files` empty |
| `empty-scope` | `failing_files(summary)` returned `()` |
| `nothing-applied` | scope non-empty, `_apply_staged_files` returned 0 |
| `applied` | `_apply_staged_files` returned a count above 0 |

The seven are mutually exclusive and are evaluated in that order, so every declared outcome is derivable and no two collapse onto the same observation.

## Scope

- `checks/config.py` parses `fix_command`. `checks/runner.py` gains `run_fix`, `parse_fix_output`, and the fix script builder.
- `temporal_activities/repair.py` deletes `_autofix_lint`, adds `_project_autofix`, `_apply_staged_files`, `_confined`, and the outcome log.
- `langgraph/ci_repair.py` gains `failing_files` and `in_repair_scope`, and its LINT instruction takes a `{fix_hint}`.
- `gates/pod_runner.py` gains a `privileged` flag and `copy_out`. `scripts/config.py` gains `gate_engine_privileged`. `gates/builtin.py`, `temporal_activities/checks.py`, and `temporal_workflows/draft_pull_request.py` thread them through.
- `config/local/checks.yaml.example` documents the key.
- Tests: `tests/unit/test_ci_repair_project_fix.py` (new), `test_ci_repair_planner.py`, `test_gate_pod_runner.py`. `test_ci_repair_autofix.py` is deleted with the code it covered.

## Grounded assumptions

- The repair path, not `run_checks`, is where a fix must land, because `commit_and_push` only fires after `repair.applied` in the `_repair` branch of `temporal_workflows/draft_pull_request.py`.
- Checks already execute inside a pod via `PodOps` in `gates/pod_runner.py`, so the fix reuses that transport.
- `run_fix` returns `ChecksFixResult(verified, exit_code, output, changed_files)`, so exit status and changed-file count are both available without a new return type.
- Buildah requires `privileged: true` under k3s on Colima, confirmed by four probe pods. `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` alone, and with seccomp Unconfined, both fail because unpacking a layer remounts the container root `MS_PRIVATE|MS_REC`.

## Testing

Happy path: a project declares `fix_command`, the lint check fails, the fix runs in the pod, and the changed files are copied back and staged. Asserted by `tests/unit/test_ci_repair_project_fix.py`.

Failure and edge paths: a project declaring no `fix_command` falls through to agent repair. A fix command that exits non-zero, or a pod that fails outright, degrades to agent repair rather than killing the workflow. A summary naming no path copies back zero files even though the fix changed files, which is the empty-scope guard. A fix touching a path outside the repair scope has that path rejected by `_confined`. A `tar` reporting a file removed by the fix command does not fail the copy-out.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `ruff check --fix .` no longer appears anywhere in `services/`, verified by `! grep -rq "ruff check --fix" services/` exiting 0.
- [ ] A project that declares `fix_command` has that command run instead, verified by `tests/unit/test_ci_repair_project_fix.py` passing.
- [ ] A project that declares no `fix_command` reaches agent repair, verified by a unit test asserting the agent repair path is taken.
- [ ] A pod failure during the fix leaves the workflow running, verified by a unit test in which the pod runner raises, asserting the agent repair path is taken.
- [ ] `_apply_staged_files` returns 0 when the scope is empty even though the fix changed files, verified by a unit test passing an empty scope with a non-empty changed list.
- [ ] `_project_autofix` emits the correct outcome name for every row of the discriminator table, verified by a parametrised unit test covering all seven outcomes.
- [ ] `ruff check services tests scripts adapters` exits 0.
- [ ] [non-codebase] A live run against `archive-massgov-pfml` reports `applied: true`.
  provenance: environment=local-colima-k3s; principal=joeoakhart; privilege_posture=broader; instrument=live-call — the gate pod runs privileged because buildah cannot unpack a layer unprivileged under k3s
- [ ] [non-codebase] That same live run modifies exactly the one file prettier flagged.
  provenance: environment=local-colima-k3s; principal=joeoakhart; privilege_posture=broader; instrument=live-call — observed from the workspace diff of the same privileged local run
- [ ] [non-codebase] That same live run reports `llm_calls: 0`.
  provenance: environment=local-colima-k3s; principal=joeoakhart; privilege_posture=broader; instrument=live-call — read from the Temporal workflow history of the same privileged local run
- [ ] [non-codebase] A re-run of the checks after that live run exits 0.
  provenance: environment=local-colima-k3s; principal=joeoakhart; privilege_posture=broader; instrument=live-call — the project checks were re-executed in the same pod image on the same privileged local stack
